statement: Let $ABC$ be a triangle. Denote the feet of the perpendiculars from $A$ to the angle bisectors of $\angle ABC$ and $\angle ACB$ by $E$, $F$ respectively. Let $I$ be the incenter of $ABC$. The circumcircles of $BIF$ and $CIE$ intersect again at $P$. Let $N$ be the midpoint of arc $BC$ containing $A$. Prove that $P$, $I$, $N$ are collinear.
Find all functions $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ that satisfy $f(x+f(y))+f(f(f(x))-y)=2x$ for all $x,y\in\mathbb{R}$.

For a positive integer $n$ let $\sigma(n)$ be the sum of divisors of $n$. Prove that there are infinitely many positive integers $m$ for which there is exactly one positive integer $n$ such that $\sigma(n)=m$.

Let $b,c,d,x,y$ be positive integers. A sequence $a_n$ is defined by $a_0=x$, $a_1=y$, and for all $n\geq 2$: $a_n=ba_{n-1}+ca_{n-2}+d$. Prove that for all positive integers $m$ there exists an index $i$ such that none of $a_i,a_{i+1},\ldots,a_{i+m-1}$ are prime.

A finite number of ants walk on a circular table of radius 1, each at speed 1. Every time two ants meet they choose a direction: one turns in that direction and the other goes opposite (both at speed 1). Assume no 3 ants are ever in the same place. The process ends when all ants fall off. (a) Can the process last forever? (b) Is there a constant $C$, independent of the number of ants, such that all ants fall off within $C$ units of time?

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with incircle $\omega$ and incenter $I$. A line $\ell$ tangent to $\omega$ intersects $BC$ at $D$ and lines $AC$, $AD$ at $E$, $F$ respectively. The common external tangents of the circumcircles of $BDF$ and $CDE$ intersect at $X$. Prove that $\angle AIX=90^\circ$.

Let $n\geq 3$ be a positive integer and let $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ be positive real numbers. The product $a_1\times a_2\times\cdots\times a_n$ is written on the board. It is known that replacing any one multiplication sign by an addition sign increases the value. Prove that replacing all multiplication signs by addition signs also increases the value.

Define the pseudo-derivative $\Delta:\mathbb{N}_{>1}\to\mathbb{N}$ as follows: for a prime $p$ and positive integer $a$, $\Delta(p^a)=ap^{a-1}$; for coprime $m,n$, $\Delta(mn)=\Delta(m)\cdot\Delta(n)$. Is it true that for any positive integer $k$ there exists a positive integer $n$ for which $\Delta^{(k)}(n)=n$ but $\Delta^{(m)}(n)\neq n$ for every $m<k$? (Here $\Delta^{(1)}(n)=\Delta(n)$ and $\Delta^{(k+1)}(n)=\Delta(\Delta^{(k)}(n))$.)

On a horizontal line $\ell$ there are $n$ blue points $b_1,\ldots,b_n$. Above that line are $n$ red points $r_1,\ldots,r_n$ such that every line through two red points contains no other red or blue point. Ayala draws $n$ segments connecting each red point to a blue point and each blue point to a red point (a bijection). Each turn, Barvaz can choose two intersecting segments $b_ir_j$ and $b_kr_l$ and replace them by $b_kr_j$ and $b_ir_l$. Prove that Barvaz can make all segments non-intersecting in at most $\binom{n}{2}$ turns.
